headline: Japanese 101 Core 30
threshold: Practice everyday Japanese with English support; lesson completion is not a proficiency credential.

lessons.title: Polite verbs for everyday actions
lessons.objective: Polite verbs for everyday actions: Practice polite ～ます forms for familiar actions; a time word such as あした can also make them describe a future action.
lessons.focus: Practice polite ～ます forms for familiar actions; a time word such as あした can also make them describe a future action.

words.es: まいにち にほんごを べんきょうします。
あきさんは としょかんで はたらきます。
あした ともだちと はなします。
words.en: Tomorrow I will talk with a friend.

words.es: せんせいの はなしを ききます。
words.en: I listen to the teacher's talk.

lessons.speaking: Role-play after class with a patient Japanese-speaking partner. Use the lesson's polite forms, ask and answer a related question, clarify one misunderstanding, and close naturally. Give brief English help when requested.

lessons.title: Common verb groups
lessons.objective: Common verb groups: Notice たべる→たべます (る-verb), のむ→のみます (う-verb), and irregular する→します and くる→きます. Learn each polite form in context.
lessons.focus: Notice たべる→たべます (る-verb), のむ→のみます (う-verb), and irregular する→します and くる→きます. Learn each polite form in context.

words.es: ひるごはんを たべます。
そのあと えいがを みます。
words.en: After that I watch a movie.

words.es: ともだちが きます。
いっしょに べんきょうします。

lessons.speaking: Role-play a shared afternoon with a patient Japanese-speaking partner. Use the lesson's polite forms, ask and answer a related question, clarify one misunderstanding, and close naturally. Give brief English help when requested.

lessons.title: Polite past and negative
lessons.objective: Polite past and negative: Use ～ました for a completed action and ～ません for a polite negative. ～ませんでした says it did not happen.
lessons.focus: Use ～ました for a completed action and ～ません for a polite negative. ～ませんでした says it did not happen.

words.es: きのう としょかんに いきました。
words.en: Yesterday I went to the library.

words.es: ほんを よみました。
でも、えいがは みませんでした。
words.en: But I did not watch a movie.

words.es: きょうは そこに いきません。
words.en: Today I am not going there.

words.es: あとで しゅくだいを します。

lessons.speaking: Role-play yesterday's plan with a patient Japanese-speaking partner. Use the lesson's polite forms, ask and answer a related question, clarify one misunderstanding, and close naturally. Give brief English help when requested.

lessons.title: Two kinds of adjective
lessons.objective: Two kinds of adjective: い-adjectives directly describe nouns. な-adjectives take な before a noun; neither agrees for gender or plural. きれい ends in い but is a な-adjective (きれいな へや).
lessons.focus: い-adjectives directly describe nouns. な-adjectives take な before a noun; neither agrees for gender or plural. きれい ends in い but is a な-adjective (きれいな へや).

words.es: この へやは おおきいです。
あの へやは ちいさいです。
ここは しずかな へやです。
となりは にぎやかです。
あたらしい つくえは きれいです。

lessons.speaking: Role-play choosing a place to study with a patient Japanese-speaking partner. Use the lesson's polite forms, ask and answer a related question, clarify one misunderstanding, and close naturally. Give brief English help when requested.

lessons.title: Whose item is it?
lessons.objective: Whose item is it?: の links a person or group to a belonging. A clear name is usually more natural than repeating a pronoun.
lessons.focus: の links a person or group to a belonging. A clear name is usually more natural than repeating a pronoun.

words.es: この かさは だれのですか。
その かばんは わたしのです。
ほんは せんせいの つくえに あります。
words.en: The book is on the teacher's desk.

words.es: ともだちの ペンも あります。
words.en: A friend's pen is there too.

lessons.speaking: Role-play found on the table with a patient Japanese-speaking partner. Use the lesson's polite forms, ask and answer a related question, clarify one misunderstanding, and close naturally. Give brief English help when requested.

lessons.title: Have and need
lessons.objective: Have and need: Use あります for possessing a thing in simple contexts. ～が ひつようです states that something is needed; ～が いります is conversational.
lessons.focus: Use あります for possessing a thing in simple contexts. ～が ひつようです states that something is needed; ～が いります is conversational.

words.es: ノートは ありますか。
じしょも ひつようですか。
words.en: Do we need a dictionary too?

words.es: いいえ、きょうは いりません。
words.en: No, we do not need one today.

words.es: えんぴつが いります。

lessons.speaking: Role-play before a lesson with a patient Japanese-speaking partner. Use the lesson's polite forms, ask and answer a related question, clarify one misunderstanding, and close naturally. Give brief English help when requested.

lessons.title: Go, come, and return
lessons.objective: Go, come, and return: いきます moves away, きます toward the speaker or reference point, and かえります returns home. に or へ marks a destination.
lessons.focus: いきます moves away, きます toward the speaker or reference point, and かえります returns home. に or へ marks a destination.

words.es: あした えきに いきます。
words.en: Tomorrow I will go to the station.

words.es: ともだちも えきに きます。
words.en: My friend will come to the station too.

words.es: そこから がっこうへ いきます。
words.en: From there we will go to school.

words.es: ごご うちに かえります。
words.en: In the afternoon I will return home.

words.es: どこへ いきますか。

lessons.speaking: Role-play meeting at the station with a patient Japanese-speaking partner. Use the lesson's polite forms, ask and answer a related question, clarify one misunderstanding, and close naturally. Give brief English help when requested.

lessons.title: What or which?
lessons.objective: What or which?: なに asks what before particles such as を; なん is common before です. どれ stands alone for which one among several, and どの modifies a noun.
lessons.focus: なに asks what before particles such as を; なん is common before です. どれ stands alone for which one among several, and どの modifies a noun.

words.es: なにを よみますか。
この ほんを よみます。
つぎは あかい ほんと しろい ほんと くろい ほん、どれを えらびますか。
words.en: Next, which will you choose: the red, white, or black book?

lessons.speaking: Role-play choosing a book with a patient Japanese-speaking partner. Use the lesson's polite forms, ask and answer a related question, clarify one misunderstanding, and close naturally. Give brief English help when requested.

lessons.title: Where, when, and why
lessons.objective: Where, when, and why: Use どこ for where, いつ for when, and どうして for why. Answer with a short reason using ～から when appropriate; here から means because, unlike the from in そこから (lesson 7).
lessons.focus: Use どこ for where, いつ for when, and どうして for why. Answer with a short reason using ～から when appropriate; here から means because, unlike the from in そこから (lesson 7).

words.es: いつ べんきょうしますか。
あした べんきょうします。
どうして あしたですか。
きょうは いそがしいですから。
どこで べんきょうしますか。
としょかんで べんきょうします。
words.en: We will study at the library.

lessons.speaking: Role-play planning a study session with a patient Japanese-speaking partner. Use the lesson's polite forms, ask and answer a related question, clarify one misunderstanding, and close naturally. Give brief English help when requested.

lessons.title: Time and schedules
lessons.objective: Time and schedules: Say a clock time with ～じ（時） and minutes with ～ふん/ぷん（分）. に marks a scheduled time; some number readings change before counters. ～ましょう suggests doing something together, while ～ましょうか asks the other person to decide.
lessons.focus: Say a clock time with ～じ（時） and minutes with ～ふん/ぷん（分）. に marks a scheduled time; some number readings change before counters. ～ましょう suggests doing something together, while ～ましょうか asks the other person to decide.

words.es: あした なんじに あいましょうか。
words.en: What time shall we meet tomorrow?

words.es: ごご さんじ じゅっぷんに あいましょう。
words.en: Let's meet at ten past three in the afternoon.

words.es: さんじ じゅっぷんは だいじょうぶです。
えきの まえで あいます。
words.en: We will meet in front of the station.

words.es: よじはんに かえります。
words.en: I will return at four thirty.

lessons.speaking: Role-play setting a meeting time with a patient Japanese-speaking partner. Use the lesson's polite forms, ask and answer a related question, clarify one misunderstanding, and close naturally. Give brief English help when requested.

lessons.title: Likes and dislikes
lessons.objective: Likes and dislikes: すき (好き) and きらい (嫌い) express likes and dislikes; the item commonly takes が. They do not follow an English verb pattern.
lessons.focus: すき (好き) and きらい (嫌い) express likes and dislikes; the item commonly takes が. They do not follow an English verb pattern.

words.es: どんな おんがくが すきですか。
words.en: What kind of music do you like?

words.es: しずかな おんがくが すきです。
えいがも すきですか。
はい、とても すきです。
words.en: Yes, I like them very much.

words.es: でも、こわい えいがは きらいです。
ほんは あまり すきじゃありません。
words.en: I do not like books very much.

lessons.speaking: Role-play music after class with a patient Japanese-speaking partner. Use the lesson's polite forms, ask and answer a related question, clarify one misunderstanding, and close naturally. Give brief English help when requested.

lessons.title: Wanting things and actions
lessons.objective: Wanting things and actions: ～がほしい marks the wanted thing with が. ～たい attaches to a verb’s ます-stem (たべます → たべたい); its object often takes を, and が is also common. At a café, use ～をください to order.
lessons.focus: ～がほしい marks the wanted thing with が. ～たい attaches to a verb’s ます-stem (たべます → たべたい); its object often takes を, and が is also common. At a café, use ～をください to order.

words.es: メニューを ください。
なにが ほしいですか。
おちゃが ほしいです。
パンも たべたいです。
words.en: I want to eat bread too.

words.es: わたしは みずを のみたいです。

lessons.speaking: Role-play friends deciding what to have at a café with a patient Japanese-speaking partner. Use the lesson's polite forms, ask and answer a related question, clarify one misunderstanding, and close naturally. Give brief English help when requested.

lessons.title: Can I? May I?
lessons.objective: Can I? May I?: できます states ability; verbs can also have potential forms such as よみます → よめます (can read). ～てもいいですか asks permission; ～てはいけません prohibits an action. Here とって is the て-form of とります; learn the two とって phrases together for now, then study the て-form in lesson 20.
lessons.focus: できます states ability; verbs can also have potential forms such as よみます → よめます (can read). ～てもいいですか asks permission; ～てはいけません prohibits an action. Here とって is the て-form of とります; learn the two とって phrases together for now, then study the て-form in lesson 20.

words.es: ここで しゃしんを とっても いいですか。
words.en: May I take a photo here?

words.es: いいえ、とっては いけません。
ほんは ここで よめますか。
words.en: Can I read a book here?

words.es: この へやに はいれますか。
はい。でも、しずかに おねがいします。

lessons.speaking: Role-play rules in the library with a patient Japanese-speaking partner. Use the lesson's polite forms, ask and answer a related question, clarify one misunderstanding, and close naturally. Give brief English help when requested.

lessons.title: What must be done
lessons.objective: What must be done: Use ～なければなりません or conversational ～ないといけません for an obligation. Both say that something must be done.
lessons.focus: Use ～なければなりません or conversational ～ないといけません for an obligation. Both say that something must be done.

words.es: かわなければなりません
いかないといけません
きっぷを かわなければなりません。
でんしゃは はちじに でます。
はやく いかないといけません。
でも、ここで ともだちを まちます。
words.en: But we will wait for a friend here.

words.es: いっしょに えきへ いきましょう。
words.en: Let's go to the station together.

lessons.speaking: Role-play before the train with a patient Japanese-speaking partner. Use the lesson's polite forms, ask and answer a related question, clarify one misunderstanding, and close naturally. Give brief English help when requested.

lessons.title: Doing everyday activities
lessons.objective: Doing everyday activities: Many activities use a noun plus します, such as べんきょうします (study) and そうじします (clean). You may also hear noun + を + します.
lessons.focus: Many activities use a noun plus します, such as べんきょうします (study) and そうじします (clean). You may also hear noun + を + します.

words.es: あさ そうじします。
ひる りょうりします。
ごご かいものします。
よる にほんごを べんきょうします。
words.en: In the evening I study Japanese.

words.es: にちようびは うんどうします。

lessons.speaking: Role-play a busy weekend with a patient Japanese-speaking partner. Use the lesson's polite forms, ask and answer a related question, clarify one misunderstanding, and close naturally. Give brief English help when requested.

lessons.title: A daily routine in order
lessons.objective: A daily routine in order: Use time words, まず (first), それから (then), and さいごに (finally) to connect ordinary actions. Seven o’clock is read しちじ.
lessons.focus: Use time words, まず (first), それから (then), and さいごに (finally) to connect ordinary actions. Seven o’clock is read しちじ.

words.es: まず、ろくじに おきます。
words.en: First I get up at six.

words.es: かおを あらいます。
それから、あさごはんを たべます。
しちじに でかけます。
さいごに、ごご うちに かえります。
words.en: Finally, I return home in the afternoon.

lessons.speaking: Role-play a weekday, morning to afternoon with a patient Japanese-speaking partner. Use the lesson's polite forms, ask and answer a related question, clarify one misunderstanding, and close naturally. Give brief English help when requested.

lessons.title: This one or that one
lessons.objective: This one or that one: これ/それ/あれ stand alone; この/その/あの must modify a noun. Choose based on distance or conversational context.
lessons.focus: これ/それ/あれ stand alone; この/その/あの must modify a noun. Choose based on distance or conversational context.

words.en: three hundred yen (ひゃく changes to びゃく)

words.es: この ノートは いくらですか。
それは にひゃくえんです。
words.en: That one is two hundred yen.

words.es: あの あおい ノートは？
あれは さんびゃくえんです。
words.en: That one is three hundred yen.

words.es: では、これを ください。
words.en: Then I will take this one, please.

lessons.speaking: Role-play at a stationery shop with a patient Japanese-speaking partner. Use the lesson's polite forms, ask and answer a related question, clarify one misunderstanding, and close naturally. Give brief English help when requested.

lessons.title: Being somewhere and doing something there
lessons.objective: Being somewhere and doing something there: に marks a place where someone or something exists; で marks the place of an action. Use position nouns such as うえ (上), した (下), and なか (中) with の.
lessons.focus: に marks a place where someone or something exists; で marks the place of an action. Use position nouns such as うえ (上), した (下), and なか (中) with の.

words.es: たなかさんは としょかんに います。
としょかんで べんきょうします。
ほんは つくえの うえに あります。
words.en: The book is on the desk.

words.es: かばんは つくえの したに あります。
words.en: The bag is under the desk.

words.es: ペンは かばんの なかに あります。
words.en: The pen is inside the bag.

lessons.speaking: Role-play where tanaka and the books are with a patient Japanese-speaking partner. Use the lesson's polite forms, ask and answer a related question, clarify one misunderstanding, and close naturally. Give brief English help when requested.

lessons.title: Plans for tomorrow
lessons.objective: Plans for tomorrow: Present polite forms can express future plans with a time word. ～つもりです states intention and ～よていです states a scheduled plan. Both follow the plain dictionary form (あいます → あう; します → する).
lessons.focus: Present polite forms can express future plans with a time word. ～つもりです states intention and ～よていです states a scheduled plan. Both follow the plain dictionary form (あいます → あう; します → する).

words.es: あした ともだちに あう つもりです。
words.en: I intend to meet a friend tomorrow.

words.es: ごご えきへ いきます。
words.en: I will go to the station in the afternoon.

words.es: らいしゅうは りょこうする よていです。
words.en: I am scheduled to travel next week.

words.es: りょこうの まえの よる、でんわします。
words.en: I will call the night before the trip.

words.es: けんさんも いく つもりですか。
words.en: Ken, do you intend to go too?

lessons.speaking: Role-play a weekend visit with a patient Japanese-speaking partner. Use the lesson's polite forms, ask and answer a related question, clarify one misunderstanding, and close naturally. Give brief English help when requested.

lessons.title: What is happening now?
lessons.objective: What is happening now?: ～ています can show an action in progress. It uses the て-form: よみます → よんで、のみます → のんで、まちます → まって. The form also includes します → して, as in なにを していますか. Some ～ています forms describe a resulting state instead; you will meet these later.
lessons.focus: ～ています can show an action in progress. It uses the て-form: よみます → よんで、のみます → のんで、まちます → まって. The form also includes します → して, as in なにを していますか. Some ～ています forms describe a resulting state instead; you will meet these later.

words.es: いま、なにを していますか。
ほんを よんでいます。
あきさんは おちゃを のんでいます。
けんさんは そとで ともだちを まっています。
words.en: Ken is waiting for a friend outside.

words.es: あきさんと せんせいは なかで はなしています。
words.en: Aki and the teacher are talking inside.

lessons.speaking: Role-play at the café window with a patient Japanese-speaking partner. Use the lesson's polite forms, ask and answer a related question, clarify one misunderstanding, and close naturally. Give brief English help when requested.

lessons.title: Know, understand, or be able to
lessons.objective: Know, understand, or be able to: しっています (知っています) is a resulting ～ています state: someone knows after learning. しりません is its usual negative. わかります means understand; できます means can do. いけます is the potential of いきます (can go).
lessons.focus: しっています (知っています) is a resulting ～ています state: someone knows after learning. しりません is its usual negative. わかります means understand; できます means can do. いけます is the potential of いきます (can go).

words.es: この みちを しっていますか。

words.en: No, I do not know it.

words.es: ちずは わかりますか。
ちずで えきまで いけます。
words.en: With the map, I can get to the station.

lessons.speaking: Role-play asking about a new town with a patient Japanese-speaking partner. Use the lesson's polite forms, ask and answer a related question, clarify one misunderstanding, and close naturally. Give brief English help when requested.

lessons.title: Compare useful choices
lessons.objective: Compare useful choices: A は B より… compares A with B. A と B と、どちらが… asks which of two; いちばん marks the top choice in a group.
lessons.focus: A は B より… compares A with B. A と B と、どちらが… asks which of two; いちばん marks the top choice in a group.

words.en: side; option (A の ほうが means A is more)

words.es: この みせは あの みせより ちかいです。
words.en: This shop is closer than that one.

words.es: でも、あの みせの ほうが しずかです。
この みせと あの みせと、どちらが べんりですか。

words.es: この みせの ほうが べんりです。えきの まえですから。
words.en: This shop is more convenient. It is in front of the station.

words.es: この まちで いちばん べんりです。
words.en: It is the most convenient in this town.

lessons.speaking: Role-play choosing a shop with a patient Japanese-speaking partner. Use the lesson's polite forms, ask and answer a related question, clarify one misunderstanding, and close naturally. Give brief English help when requested.

lessons.title: The object of an action
lessons.objective: The object of an action: を marks the direct object of many actions. Once the object is clear, Japanese can omit it naturally where English uses it or them. も can replace を when adding another object, as in ペンも いれます.
lessons.focus: を marks the direct object of many actions. Once the object is clear, Japanese can omit it naturally where English uses it or them. も can replace を when adding another object, as in ペンも いれます.

words.es: ほんを かばんに いれます。
words.en: I put the book in the bag.
I put a pen in too.

words.es: かぎを さがしています。
words.en: I am looking for my keys.

words.es: もう わすれません。
words.en: I will not forget them again.

lessons.speaking: Role-play packing a bag with a patient Japanese-speaking partner. Use the lesson's polite forms, ask and answer a related question, clarify one misunderstanding, and close naturally. Give brief English help when requested.

lessons.title: Giving and receiving
lessons.objective: Giving and receiving: に marks the recipient with あげます and くれます. With もらいます, the giver takes に or から. The three verbs differ by whose perspective the sentence takes.
lessons.focus: に marks the recipient with あげます and くれます. With もらいます, the giver takes に or から. The three verbs differ by whose perspective the sentence takes.

words.es: おれいを いいます
わたしは ともだちに ノートを あげます。
words.en: I give my friend a notebook.

words.es: ともだちは わたしに コピーを くれます。
words.en: My friend gives me a copy.

words.es: せんせいから しりょうを もらいました。
words.en: I received materials from the teacher.

words.es: その しりょうを あきさんに あげます。
words.en: I will give those materials to Aki.

words.es: あきさんは おれいを いいます。

lessons.speaking: Role-play sharing notebooks and handouts with a patient Japanese-speaking partner. Use the lesson's polite forms, ask and answer a related question, clarify one misunderstanding, and close naturally. Give brief English help when requested.

lessons.title: People as objects or destinations
lessons.objective: People as objects or destinations: Use に with あいます for the person you meet. To go to a person, say [person] の ところに いきます. Use を with よびます (call over) or てつだいます (help). The particle depends on the Japanese verb.
lessons.focus: Use に with あいます for the person you meet. To go to a person, say [person] の ところに いきます. Use を with よびます (call over) or てつだいます (help). The particle depends on the Japanese verb.

words.es: えきで ともだちに あいます。
words.en: I will meet my friend at the station.

words.es: ともだちを よびます。
ひとが こまっています。
その ひとの ところに いきます。
words.en: I go over to that person.

words.es: てつだいましょうか。かばんを もちましょうか。
words.en: May I help? Shall I carry the bag?

lessons.speaking: Role-play helping a visitor with a patient Japanese-speaking partner. Use the lesson's polite forms, ask and answer a related question, clarify one misunderstanding, and close naturally. Give brief English help when requested.

lessons.title: A completed past event
lessons.objective: A completed past event: Review polite ～ました for completed actions. You already met it in Core lesson 3; here use it to tell a short sequence about yesterday. Plain past forms such as いった are casual and will be taught separately.
lessons.focus: Review polite ～ました for completed actions. You already met it in Core lesson 3; here use it to tell a short sequence about yesterday. Plain past forms such as いった are casual and will be taught separately.

words.es: きのう がっこうへ いきました。
あたらしい ほんを かいました。
ひる ともだちと はなしました。
words.en: At noon I spoke with a friend.

words.es: あとで しゅくだいを しました。
よる てがみを かきました。
words.en: At night I wrote a letter.

lessons.speaking: Role-play yesterday at school with a patient Japanese-speaking partner. Use the lesson's polite forms, ask and answer a related question, clarify one misunderstanding, and close naturally. Give brief English help when requested.

lessons.title: Polite past of going, coming, doing and being
lessons.objective: Polite past of going, coming, doing and being: Every polite verb forms the past with ～ます → ～ました: いきます → いきました, きます → きました, します → しました. Nouns and な-adjectives take でした, as in りょこうでした and きれいでした. い-adjectives change themselves: たのしい → たのしかったです. The irregular plain past forms いった, きた and した come later.
lessons.focus: Every polite verb forms the past with ～ます → ～ました: いきます → いきました, きます → きました, します → しました. Nouns and な-adjectives take でした, as in りょこうでした and きれいでした. い-adjectives change themselves: たのしい → たのしかったです. The irregular plain past forms いった, きた and した come later.

words.es: せんしゅう きょうとに いきました。
words.en: Last week I went to Kyoto.

words.es: ともだちも いっしょに いきました。
ふたりで りょこうを しました。
まちは とても きれいでした。
たのしい りょこうでした。

lessons.speaking: Role-play a trip and a report with a patient Japanese-speaking partner. Use the lesson's polite forms, ask and answer a related question, clarify one misunderstanding, and close naturally. Give brief English help when requested.

lessons.title: An old habit and one event
lessons.objective: An old habit and one event: Japanese does not need a separate form for “used to.” Use よく or いつも with past forms for habits, and a specific time for a single event.
lessons.focus: Japanese does not need a separate form for “used to.” Use よく or いつも with past forms for habits, and a specific time for a single event.

words.es: むかし、よく がっこうまで あるきました。
words.en: I often walked to school long ago.

words.es: いつも ともだちと いきました。
words.en: I always went with a friend.

words.es: きのうは ひとりで あるきました。
いまは でんしゃで いきます。
でも、ときどき あるきます。

lessons.speaking: Role-play then and now with a patient Japanese-speaking partner. Use the lesson's polite forms, ask and answer a related question, clarify one misunderstanding, and close naturally. Give brief English help when requested.

lessons.title: Purpose and reason
lessons.objective: Purpose and reason: Purpose can use a verb’s ます-stem + に いきます (べんきょうします → べんきょうしに) or noun + の ために. Reason can use ～から or ～ので.
lessons.focus: Purpose can use a verb’s ます-stem + に いきます (べんきょうします → べんきょうしに) or noun + の ために. Reason can use ～から or ～ので.

words.es: べんきょうしに としょかんへ いきます。
words.en: I am going to the library to study.

words.es: しけんの ために ほんを よみます。
words.en: I read a book for the exam.

words.es: どうして きょうは でんしゃですか。
あめが ふっていますから。
あめなので、でんしゃで いきます。
words.en: Since it is raining, I will go by train.

lessons.speaking: Role-play why visit the library? with a patient Japanese-speaking partner. Use the lesson's polite forms, ask and answer a related question, clarify one misunderstanding, and close naturally. Give brief English help when requested.

lessons.title: Connect and review ideas
lessons.objective: Connect and review ideas: そして adds, でも contrasts, それから sequences, and だから gives a result. でかける is the plain form of でかけます before よてい. Make a short coherent account and review particles and polite forms.
lessons.focus: そして adds, でも contrasts, それから sequences, and だから gives a result. でかける is the plain form of でかけます before よてい. Make a short coherent account and review particles and polite forms.

words.es: きょうは ともだちと でかける よていでした。
words.en: Today I had planned to go out with a friend.

words.es: でも、あめが ふっています。
だから、きょうは でかけません。
words.en: So I will not go out today.

words.es: それから、ともだちに でんわします。
words.en: Then I will call my friend.

words.es: そして、うちで いっしょに べんきょうします。
words.en: And we will study together at home.

lessons.speaking: Role-play a changed plan with a patient Japanese-speaking partner. Use the lesson's polite forms, ask and answer a related question, clarify one misunderstanding, and close naturally. Give brief English help when requested.
